forces.title: Operator capex shifts from 5G coverage to capacity and densification.
forces.description: CareEdge Ratings projects telecom operators' capex intensity to moderate from 22% in FY26 to 19% in FY27, as the initial aggressive 5G rollout phase concludes. The strategic shift is towards selective capacity augmentation and fibre densification rather than broad coverage expansion. For passive infrastructure, this signals a changing demand profile: reduced need for new greenfield tower sites but sustained investment in upgrades, multi-tenancy, and fibre backhaul to existing infrastructure.
forces.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

forces.title: India's 5G infrastructure market set for exponential long-term growth.
forces.description: The 5G infrastructure market in India is projected to grow from US$14 billion in 2025 to US$574.4 billion by 2035, exhibiting a 45% CAGR, according to IBEF. This rapid expansion, driven by widespread 5G adoption, substantial investments, and large-scale deployments, creates immense demand for new passive infrastructure. This includes tower sites, small cell deployments, distributed antenna systems, and robust fibre backhaul to support the ultra-dense and high-capacity requirements of 5G networks.

forces.title: Government drives telecom infrastructure expansion with substantial funding.
forces.description: The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated over US$8.37 billion to the Department of Telecommunications, alongside additional USOF funding, underscoring a strong focus on rural connectivity and telecom infrastructure expansion. Furthermore, US$17.0 billion (INR 1.50 lakh crore) is allocated for the BharatNet programme to connect 260,000 Gram Panchayats with high-speed broadband, bolstering 5G deployment and future 6G services. These continuous government initiatives and investments serve as a robust tailwind for the towers and passive infrastructure sector, ensuring sustained demand, particularly in underserved regions.

forces.title: Accelerated 5G BTS installations necessitate proportional passive infrastructure growth.
forces.description: India has achieved one of the world's fastest 5G rollouts, with approximately 5.23 lakh 5G Base Transceiver Stations (BTSs) installed nationwide by February 2026. Each BTS requires foundational passive infrastructure, including tower space, power supply, and robust backhaul connectivity, often via optical fibre. This aggressive deployment of active network components directly translates into a significant and ongoing demand for the underlying passive infrastructure, driving expansion and densification efforts for tower companies.

forces.title: Expanding fibre network deployment critical for tower backhaul and densification.
forces.description: The Indian government aims to deploy nearly 7 lakh km of optical fibre (OFC) and achieve 1.5 crore FTTH connections by FY2026. This extensive fibre optic rollout, while serving direct broadband connectivity, is indispensable for providing high-capacity, low-latency backhaul for mobile towers, especially for demanding 5G and upcoming 6G networks. It ensures network performance and capacity, directly boosting demand for fibre-to-the-tower and other associated passive infrastructure components.

forces.title: Exponential mobile data consumption drives continuous network capacity demand.
forces.description: India holds the distinction of being the largest consumer of mobile data globally, with wireless data usage increasing from 69,090 PB in Q.E. Sep-25 to 73,324 PB in Q.E. Dec-25. Average monthly mobile data usage per smartphone, already at 37 GB, is expected to nearly double to 70 GB by 2031. This exponential growth in data consumption necessitates continuous network capacity augmentation, densification, and upgrades, thereby sustaining robust demand for tower and passive infrastructure services to handle the increasing traffic.

forces.title: Independent tower companies commit substantial capex to network support.
forces.description: CRISIL Ratings projects independent telecom tower companies will invest Rs 21,000 crore (US$ 2.42 billion) between FY25 and FY26. This significant capital outlay is dedicated to supporting telecom operators in expanding rural network coverage and enhancing urban service quality. This commitment highlights strong internal investment within the passive infrastructure sector to meet evolving network demands, ensuring continued infrastructure growth and upgrades essential for advanced connectivity across India.

viewpoints.title: Telecom capex shifts from 5G coverage to capacity and densification.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings projects Indian telecom operators' capex intensity to moderate from 22% in FY26 to 19% in FY27, as the peak 5G rollout phase concludes. The strategic shift is towards selective capacity augmentation and fibre densification rather than broad coverage expansion. For tower and passive infrastructure companies, this implies a potential slowdown in new greenfield tower construction but continued, strong demand for upgrades, multi-tenancy on existing sites, and extensive fibre backhaul, supporting long-term annuity-like revenue streams.

viewpoints.title: Independent tower companies to significantly invest in rural and urban network support.
viewpoints.description: CRISIL Ratings projects independent telecom tower companies will invest Rs 21,000 crore (US$ 2.42 billion) between FY25 and FY26. This substantial investment is aimed at bolstering telecom companies' efforts to expand rural network coverage and enhance service quality in urban areas. This highlights a positive outlook for the passive infrastructure sector, driven by ongoing network expansion and quality improvement initiatives across India, ensuring robust demand for tower site development and upgrades.

viewpoints.title: India's 5G infrastructure market to experience massive long-term growth.
viewpoints.description: The IBEF report highlights that the 5G infrastructure market in India is forecast to surge from US$14 billion (Rs. 1,19,966 crore) in 2025 to US$574.4 billion (Rs. 49,18,606 crore) by 2035, demonstrating a remarkable 45% CAGR. This exponential growth, driven by rapid adoption and significant investments, signals a robust and expanding demand for the underlying passive infrastructure components essential for a dense 5G network, including tower sites, small cells, and extensive fibre backhaul.
